extension.description: Reviews shell launches that expose a browser to automation: remote debugging, the user's real profile, WebDriver servers and browser automation CLIs.
extension.name: Browser automation launch protection

permissions.description: Identifies a Chromium-family browser started with a remote debugging port or pipe. Any local process that reaches that port can read and drive every page, cookie and session in the browser.
permissions.label: Browser remote debugging launch
safer_guidance: Let the browser MCP server start its own isolated browser instead of exposing a debugging port.
If a debugging port is needed, use a fresh temporary --user-data-dir and close the browser when done.

permissions.description: Identifies a Chromium-family browser started with one of the user's own profiles: a named --profile-directory without a separate --user-data-dir, or --user-data-dir set to the browser's default profile location. That profile holds the user's signed-in sessions, saved passwords and cookies.
permissions.label: Browser launch with a real profile
safer_guidance: Start the browser with a fresh temporary --user-data-dir so no signed-in session is exposed.

permissions.description: Identifies a WebDriver server such as chromedriver, geckodriver or msedgedriver. The server listens on a local port and lets any client that reaches it start and drive a browser.
permissions.label: WebDriver server
safer_guidance: Prefer a browser MCP server that starts its own isolated browser over a standalone WebDriver server.

permissions.description: Identifies automation CLIs that open, record or capture a browser: playwright codegen, open, screenshot, pdf and the cr, ff and wk shortcuts, and @puppeteer/browsers launch. Install commands are not matched here; package review handles them.
permissions.label: Browser automation CLI
safer_guidance: Run the automation against a local development server or a disposable test site.
